definitions.author: Emile Durkheim
definitions.definition: A condition of normlessness where social norms degrade or break down, leading to a lack of moral regulation in society.
definitions.reusable_context: Useful for Sociology Paper 1 & GS 1 questions on social disorder, suicide, rapid industrialization, and modern crime.

definitions.author: Supreme Court of India (Kesavananda Bharati Case 1973)
definitions.definition: Judicial principle that certain fundamental features of the Constitution (Democracy, Federalism, Rule of Law, Judicial Review, Secularism) cannot be altered or destroyed through Parliamentary amendments under Article 368.
definitions.reusable_context: Essential for GS 2 questions on Constitutional Amendments, Judicial Review, and Separation of Powers.

definitions.author: 2nd ARC / Philosophical Ethics
definitions.definition: Strict adherence to the highest standards of honesty, integrity, transparency, and ethical conduct in public administration.
definitions.reusable_context: Core term for GS 4 Ethics questions on corruption, administrative integrity, and public service values.

definitions.author: UN Disaster Risk Reduction (2015-2030)
definitions.definition: Voluntary 15-year agreement prioritizing understanding disaster risk, strengthening risk governance, investing in resilience, and 'Building Back Better' in recovery.
definitions.reusable_context: Crucial hook for GS 3 Disaster Management questions.

thinker_quotes.quote: The world has enough for everyone's need, but not for everyone's greed.
thinker_quotes.context: Ideal quote for GS 3 Environment, GS 4 Ethics, and Essay papers on sustainability and consumerism.

thinker_quotes.quote: Constitutional morality is not a natural sentiment. It has to be cultivated. We must realize that our people have yet to learn it.
thinker_quotes.context: High-impact opening quote for GS 2 Polity & Governance questions.

thinker_quotes.quote: In law a man is guilty when he violates the rights of others. In ethics he is guilty if he only thinks of doing so.
thinker_quotes.context: Great opening quote for GS 4 Ethics theory questions.

thinker_quotes.quote: The history of all hitherto existing society is the history of class struggles.
thinker_quotes.context: Introductory hook for Sociology stratification or historical change questions.

intro_templates.template: Federalism in India is a constitutional compromise between central unity and regional autonomy. As the Supreme Court highlighted in the S.R. Bommai case, federalism is a basic feature of the Constitution, requiring 'Cooperative and Competitive Federalism' to address multi-dimensional governance challenges.

Inclusive growth goes beyond aggregate GDP metrics to ensure equitable distribution of economic opportunities, poverty reduction, financial inclusion, and social empowerment, aligning with SDG 1 (No Poverty) and SDG 10 (Reduced Inequalities).

Throughout human history, great intellectual leaps have originated not from static consensus, but from the courageous questioning of established dogmas. As Socrates posited, 'An unexamined life is not worth living'...

outro_templates.template: Thus, fostering probity in governance requires a dual approach: institutional mechanisms (L Lokpal, Whistleblower Protection, E-governance) combined with internal moral grounding (Niti and Niyati) among public servants to fulfill the constitutional vision of a welfare state.

Moving forward, India's pathway must balance developmental aspirations with environmental stewardship by embedding climate resilience into infrastructure, fulfilling Panchamrit commitments, and embracing the LiFE (Lifestyle for Environment) global movement.

diagrams.title: GS 4 Ethical Dilemma Resolution Framework
diagrams.description: Flowchart showing: Input Dilemma -> Stakeholder Mapping -> Identification of Options -> Ethical Justification (Utilitarian vs Deontological vs Virtue Ethics) -> Final Action Plan.
diagrams.reusable_context: Draw for any GS 4 Ethics Case Study.

diagrams.title: GS 2 Separation of Powers Triad
diagrams.description: Triangle diagram showing Legislature (Law Making), Executive (Law Implementation), and Judiciary (Law Interpretation) with double-headed check-and-balance arrows.
diagrams.reusable_context: Draw for questions on Judicial Activism, Executive Orders, or Parliamentary Oversight.
